bull.b: Recurring revenue is growing faster than total sales, improving mix toward contracted and repeatable income. This can support better forecasting, customer retention, and higher-margin growth as the platform scales across transportation and public-safety deployments.

Higher gross margins and reduced operating expenses show operating leverage in the business model. Continued savings, product mix improvement, and recurring revenue growth provide a credible foundation for management's targeted adjusted-EBITDA profitability in H2 2026.

Material deleveraging reduces financial risk and provides more balance-sheet flexibility while the company works toward profitability. Positive equity offers additional support, although sustained losses still require careful capital management over the medium term.

bear.b: Rekor remains materially unprofitable, so revenue growth has not yet translated into durable earnings. The company must execute further cost reductions and expand efficiently; otherwise continued losses could erode equity and delay self-funded growth.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business still consumes capital to sustain operations. Although burn has improved, ongoing funding needs or additional cost actions could constrain investment, increase financing dependence, and pressure execution.

Regulatory scrutiny around data retention, sharing, and access can slow adoption of ALPR solutions and raise compliance costs. Unpredictable government purchasing compounds the issue, making bookings, contract timing, and medium-term revenue conversion harder to forecast.
